title: Anchoring and the Psychology of Negotiation
explainer: Kahneman and Tversky's heuristics-and-biases research in the 1970s showed that an arbitrary first number a person hears measurably pulls their later numeric judgments toward it — the anchoring effect. It is directly relevant to salary and scope negotiations: whoever states a figure first tends to drag the final outcome toward that figure, which is why common negotiation advice ('let the other side name a number first') rests on real experimental psychology rather than folklore.
